preamble: Following the atlas convention for ∅ → nasal-vowel cells, this entry records the case where a nasal consonant is deleted and leaves its nasality on a preceding mid front vowel, yielding [ẽ]. Nothing is actually inserted, so the process is better described as e → ẽ with loss of the nasal (see e_to_e_nas). The French example previously listed here was wrong for this cell: Latin panem became French pain [pɛ̃], an open-mid [ɛ̃] reached by way of an a + yod diphthong, so the outcome is not [ẽ]. Portuguese is the clearest case: a coda nasal after e was absorbed into the vowel, giving [ẽ] before consonants and the nasal diphthong [ẽj̃] word-finally in Brazilian Portuguese.

examples.note: The coda /m/ before a stop is not realized as a separate segment; the vowel carries the nasality in both European and Brazilian Portuguese.
The final nasal was absorbed into the vowel, which then diphthongized. European Portuguese has [ˈsɐ̃j̃].
